source.text: Ταῦτα αὐτοῦ λαλοῦντος αὐτοῖς ἰδοὺ ἄρχων εἷς ἐλθὼν προσεκύνει αὐτῷ λέγων ὅτι Ἡ θυγάτηρ μου ἄρτι ἐτελεύτησεν· ἀλλὰ ἐλθὼν ἐπίθες τὴν χεῖρά σου ἐπ’ αὐτήν, καὶ ζήσεται.

records.literal_gloss: These things of him speaking to them behold, a ruler one having come was kneeling to him saying, The daughter of me just died; but having come lay the hand of you on her, and she will live.

en.L: While {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was saying these things to them, look, a ruler came and knelt before {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, saying, "My daughter has just died, but come and lay {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand on her, and she will live."
en.B: While Jesus was still speaking, a leader came and knelt in front of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. "My daughter has just died," he said. "But come and put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand on her, and she will live."
en.R: While Jesus was saying these things, a leader came to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He bowed down in front of Jesus and said, "My daughter has just died. But come and put {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} hand on her, and she will live again."

es.L: Mientras {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} les decía estas cosas, mira, un jefe vino y se postró ante {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, diciendo: «Mi hija acaba de morir; pero ven, pon {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano sobre ella, y vivirá».
es.B: Mientras Jesús todavía hablaba, llegó un dirigente y se arrodilló delante de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. «Mi hija acaba de morir —dijo—. Pero ven, pon {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano sobre ella, y vivirá».
es.R: Mientras Jesús decía estas cosas, llegó un dirigente y se acercó a {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Se inclinó delante de Jesús y dijo: «Mi hija acaba de morir. Pero ven y pon {{deity_pronoun:tu|Tu}} mano sobre ella, y volverá a vivir».

fr.L: Pendant qu’{{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} leur disait ces choses, voici, un chef vint et se prosterna devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}, disant : « Ma fille vient de mourir ; mais viens, pose {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main sur elle, et elle vivra. »
fr.B: Jésus parlait encore quand un chef vint s’agenouiller devant {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. « Ma fille vient de mourir, dit-il. Mais viens poser {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main sur elle, et elle vivra. »
fr.R: Pendant que Jésus disait ces choses, un chef est venu vers {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}}. Il s’est mis à genoux devant Jésus et il a dit : « Ma fille vient de mourir. Mais viens poser {{deity_pronoun:ta|Ta}} main sur elle, et elle vivra de nouveau. »

sw.L: Alipokuwa akisema nao mambo haya, tazama, kiongozi mmoja akaja, akapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, akisema, "Binti yangu amefariki punde hivi; lakini njoo, umwekee mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, naye ataishi."
sw.B: Yesu alipokuwa bado anazungumza, kiongozi mmoja alifika, akapiga magoti mbele {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}. Akasema, "Binti yangu amefariki hivi punde. Lakini njoo umwekee mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, naye ataishi."
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akisema mambo hayo, kiongozi mmoja alikuja {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Aliinama mbele ya Yesu, akasema, "Binti yangu amekufa sasa hivi. Lakini njoo umwekee mkono {{deity_pronoun:wako|Wako}}, naye ataishi tena."

vi.L: Khi {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} đang nói những điều ấy với họ, kìa, một người lãnh đạo đến quỳ lạy {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Con gái tôi vừa mới chết; nhưng xin Thầy đến đặt tay trên nó, thì nó sẽ sống."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu còn đang nói thì có một người lãnh đạo đến quỳ trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và thưa: "Con gái tôi vừa mới chết. Nhưng xin Thầy đến đặt tay trên cháu, thì cháu sẽ sống."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu đang nói những điều ấy thì có một người lãnh đạo nhà hội đến. Ông quỳ xuống trước mặt {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} và nói: "Con gái tôi vừa mới chết. Nhưng xin Thầy đến đặt tay trên cháu, cháu sẽ sống lại."

ko.L: 그분이 그들에게 이것들을 말씀하고 계실 때에, 보라, 한 지도자가 와서 그분께 엎드려 절하며 말했다. "제 딸이 방금 죽었습니다. 그러나 오셔서 그 아이 위에 손을 얹어 주십시오. 그러면 그 아이가 살 것입니다."
ko.B: 예수께서 아직 이 말씀을 하고 계실 때에, 한 지도자가 와서 예수께 엎드려 절하며 말했다. "제 딸이 방금 죽었습니다. 그러나 오셔서 그 아이에게 손을 얹어 주십시오. 그러면 살아날 것입니다."
ko.R: 예수께서 이런 말씀을 하고 계실 때, 회당을 이끄는 지도자 한 사람이 왔다. 그는 예수 앞에 엎드려 절하고 말했다. "제 딸이 방금 죽었습니다. 그렇지만 오셔서 그 아이에게 손을 얹어 주십시오. 그러면 그 아이가 다시 살아날 것입니다."

pt.L: Enquanto {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}} lhes dizia essas coisas, eis que um chefe veio e se ajoelhou diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, dizendo: "Minha filha acaba de morrer; mas vem, põe a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão sobre ela, e ela viverá."
pt.B: Enquanto Jesus ainda falava, um líder chegou e se ajoelhou diante {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. "Minha filha acabou de morrer", disse ele. "Mas vem e põe a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão sobre ela, e ela viverá."
pt.R: Enquanto Jesus dizia essas coisas, um líder foi até {{deity_pronoun:ele|Ele}}. O homem se curvou diante de Jesus e disse: "Minha filha acabou de morrer. Mas vem e põe a {{deity_pronoun:tua|Tua}} mão sobre ela, e ela vai viver de novo."

am.L: እርሱ ይህን ሲነግራቸው ሳለ፣ እነሆ፣ አንድ አለቃ መጥቶ እየሰገደለት እንዲህ አለ፦ «ሴት ልጄ አሁን ሞተች፤ ነገር ግን መጥተህ እጅህን በእርሷ ላይ ጫን፤ በሕይወትም ትኖራለች።»
am.B: ኢየሱስ ገና ይህን እየተናገረ ሳለ አንድ አለቃ መጥቶ በፊቱ ተንበረከከ። «ሴት ልጄ አሁን ገና ሞተች» አለው፤ «ነገር ግን መጥተህ እጅህን ጫንባት፤ በሕይወትም ትኖራለች።»
am.R: ኢየሱስ ይህን እየተናገረ ሳለ አንድ አለቃ ወደ እርሱ መጣ። በኢየሱስ ፊት ሰግዶ እንዲህ አለ፦ «ሴት ልጄ አሁን ገና ሞተች። ነገር ግን መጥተህ እጅህን ጫንባት፤ እንደ ገና በሕይወት ትኖራለች።»

decisions.choice: a ruler: a leader of the synagogue
decisions.reason: Matthew says only "a ruler". Mark 5:22 and Luke 8:41 name him Jairus, a leader of the synagogue.
Matthew tells the story briefly, and the father's faith asks for life from the dead.
As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.
A new section begins here, so Balanced and Readable name Jesus.

decisions.choice: narration in the passé simple (L, B) and the passé composé (R); Matthew's historic presents kept as presents at Literal ("dit", 9:28, 9:37)
decisions.reason: As in John and the other Gospels: the passé simple is the tense of written narrative and suits a public reading; Readable uses the passé composé, as French is spoken and taught. Speech keeps its own tenses at every level. This holds for the whole passage.
Matthew does not say what the man led; the meaning note (m1) says a synagogue leader is likely, but French keeps Matthew's general word rather than bring in Mark's and Luke's "chef de synagogue".

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on free pronouns and possessives (mbele yake, mkono wako, kwake)
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Swahili carries most pronouns in the verb ("alipokuwa", "walimfuata"), and a prefix cannot take a capital, so the setting applies only to free pronouns and possessives, as in John and Mark. Swahili therefore has fewer spans than English throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: deity_pronoun spans only on separate pronouns and possessives: ante él, tu mano
alternatives: a span on every pronoun the English marks
decisions.reason: Spanish usually leaves the subject pronoun out ("dijo", "entró") and joins some object pronouns to the verb ("pídanle"), where there is nothing separate to capitalise. So the setting covers fewer words than in English. This holds for the whole passage.

The term used across the New Testament drafts for the Greek "look": Literal keeps it as the everyday "mira" rather than the old "he aquí"; Balanced and Readable leave it out, as the English does. The same in verses 20 and 32.

decisions.choice: "người lãnh đạo" (L, B); "người lãnh đạo nhà hội" (R) for the ruler
decisions.reason: The meaning decision reads the ruler as a leader of the synagogue, as Jairus is in Mark 5:22, where Vietnamese has "người lãnh đạo nhà hội". Literal and Balanced keep Matthew's shorter word; Readable names the office.

decisions.choice: "Thầy" for "your" and "tôi" for "my" in the ruler's words; "nó" (L), "cháu" (B, R) for his daughter
decisions.reason: As Jairus in Mark 5:23: he comes to Jesus with respect but is not shown as a disciple, so he says "Thầy" and "tôi". "Thầy" is a noun of address and takes no setting span. A father speaking of his child to an elder says "cháu"; Literal keeps the plain pronoun.

Matthew says only "a ruler"; the meaning decision says he led a synagogue. Literal and Balanced keep Matthew's general word, and Readable says what he led, as the Korean Mark 5:22 Readable does. "회당장" stays Mark's word, where the Greek has it.

decisions.choice: The ruler speaks to Jesus in 합쇼체 with "제 딸" and "오셔서 ... 얹어 주십시오"; no deity_pronoun spans in Korean, through this passage
decisions.reason: People speak to Jesus in 합쇼체 (docs/korean-style.md section 4), as Jairus does in the Korean Mark 5:23. Korean has no capital letters, so respect for Jesus is carried by -시-, 께서 and 그분 instead of the deity_pronoun setting (section 7).

The father speaks to Jesus, so he says "tu" (docs/portuguese-style.md, section 4): "vem", "põe", "tua". "Você" would be too casual for a man kneeling before Jesus, and "o senhor" would blur with "Senhor" as a title.

Portuguese has no everyday word that matches the English Literal "look" in narration ("olhe" speaks to someone). "Eis que" is the Portuguese form of the word and still widely read, so Literal keeps it; Balanced and Readable carry its force in the flow of the sentence, as the English does.

The Ethiopic script has no capital letters, so the setting that capitalises pronouns for God and Jesus has nothing to change in Amharic; the pronouns (እርሱ, እሱ, the verb endings) are written once, with no span.

A man of rank speaking to Jesus might use the honorific እርስዎ in ordinary life, but the Greek has the plain singular, and this translation gives everyone who speaks to Jesus the Bible's familiar አንተ; a reviewer may prefer እርስዎ for petitioners who do not yet know him.

source.text: καὶ ἐγερθεὶς ὁ Ἰησοῦς ἠκολούθει αὐτῷ καὶ οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: And having got up the Jesus followed him and the disciples of him.

en.L: And Jesus got up and followed him, and [so did] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.
en.B: Jesus got up and went with him, and so did {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} disciples.
en.R: So Jesus got up and went with him. His followers went too.

es.L: Y Jesús, levantándose, lo seguía, y [también] {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos.
es.B: Jesús se levantó y fue con él, y también {{deity_pronoun:sus|Sus}} discípulos.
es.R: Entonces Jesús se levantó y se fue con él. Sus seguidores también fueron.

fr.L: Et Jésus, s’étant levé, le suivit, ainsi que {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples.
fr.B: Jésus se leva et partit avec lui, et {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} disciples aussi.
fr.R: Alors Jésus s’est levé et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} est parti avec lui. Ses disciples sont venus aussi.

sw.L: Na Yesu akainuka, akamfuata, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} [pia].
sw.B: Yesu aliinuka, akaenda pamoja naye, na wanafunzi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} pia.
sw.R: Basi Yesu aliinuka, akaenda pamoja naye. Wafuasi {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} nao walikwenda.

vi.L: Và Đức Giê-xu đứng dậy đi theo ông, và các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} [cũng vậy].
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu đứng dậy đi với ông, các môn đồ {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng đi theo.
vi.R: Vậy Đức Giê-xu đứng dậy và đi với ông. Các môn đồ của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} cũng đi theo.

ko.L: 그러자 예수께서 일어나 그를 따라가셨고, 그분의 제자들도 [따라갔다].
ko.B: 예수께서 일어나 그와 함께 가셨고, 제자들도 함께 갔다.
ko.R: 그래서 예수께서 일어나 그 사람과 함께 가셨다. 제자들도 따라갔다.

pt.L: E Jesus se levantou e o seguiu, e [também] os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos.
pt.B: Jesus se levantou e foi com ele, e os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} discípulos também.
pt.R: Então Jesus se levantou e foi com o homem. Os {{deity_pronoun:seus|Seus}} seguidores foram também.

am.L: ኢየሱስም ተነሥቶ ተከተለው፤ ደቀ መዛሙርቱም [ተከተሉት]።
am.B: ኢየሱስም ተነሥቶ ከእርሱ ጋር ሄደ፤ ደቀ መዛሙርቱም እንዲሁ።
am.R: ስለዚህ ኢየሱስ ተነሥቶ ከአለቃው ጋር ሄደ። ደቀ መዛሙርቱም አብረው ሄዱ።

decisions.reason: Here the verb simply means going along with someone.

The English Readable says "followers"; French keeps "les disciples" at every level, as the style guide and the French of Mark and Luke do. The word is well known in French. This holds for the whole passage.

decisions.choice: ደቀ መዛሙርት at every level, Readable included
alternatives: ተከታዮች (followers), as the English Readable says
decisions.reason: ደቀ መዛሙርት is the ordinary Amharic word for a teacher's disciples, known to every reader, so Readable keeps it; ተከታዮች would make them sound like supporters of a cause.

source.text: Καὶ ἰδοὺ γυνὴ αἱμορροοῦσα δώδεκα ἔτη προσελθοῦσα ὄπισθεν ἥψατο τοῦ κρασπέδου τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ·

records.literal_gloss: And behold, a woman suffering bleeding twelve years having come behind touched the fringe of the garment of him;

en.L: And look, a woman who had been suffering from bleeding for twelve years came up behind [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}] and touched the fringe of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garment,
en.B: Then a woman came up behind {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. For twelve years she had suffered from bleeding. She touched the tassel on {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak.
en.R: Then a woman came up behind Jesus. She had been bleeding for twelve years. She touched the edge of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes.

es.L: Y mira, una mujer que sufría de hemorragias [desde hacía] doce años, llegándose por detrás [de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}], tocó la franja de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto;
es.B: Entonces una mujer se acercó por detrás de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Hacía doce años que padecía hemorragias. Tocó la borla de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto.
es.R: Entonces una mujer se acercó a Jesús por detrás. Hacía doce años que sangraba. Tocó el borde de {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa.

fr.L: Et voici, une femme qui souffrait d’une perte de sang depuis douze ans s’approcha par-derrière et toucha la frange de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} vêtement,
fr.B: Alors une femme s’approcha de {{deity_pronoun:lui|Lui}} par-derrière. Depuis douze ans, elle souffrait de pertes de sang. Elle toucha la frange de {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} manteau.
fr.R: Alors une femme s’est approchée de Jésus par-derrière. Elle perdait du sang depuis douze ans. Elle a touché le bord de {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements.

sw.L: Na tazama, mwanamke mmoja mwenye ugonjwa wa kutokwa damu kwa miaka kumi na miwili, akimkaribia kwa nyuma, aligusa kishada cha vazi {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}};
sw.B: Kisha mwanamke mmoja alimjia kwa nyuma. Kwa miaka kumi na miwili alikuwa ameugua ugonjwa wa kutokwa damu. Akagusa kishada cha joho {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}}.
sw.R: Kisha mwanamke mmoja alimjia Yesu kwa nyuma. Alikuwa akitokwa damu kwa miaka kumi na miwili. Aligusa ukingo wa nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}}.

vi.L: Và kìa, một người phụ nữ bị ra huyết đã mười hai năm đến phía sau [{{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}] và chạm vào tua áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}},
vi.B: Bấy giờ có một người phụ nữ đến phía sau {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}. Bà đã bị bệnh rong huyết mười hai năm. Bà chạm vào tua áo choàng của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.
vi.R: Lúc ấy có một người phụ nữ đến phía sau Đức Giê-xu. Bà bị bệnh ra máu đã mười hai năm. Bà chạm vào mép áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}.

ko.L: 그리고 보라, 열두 해 동안 피가 흐르는 [병을] 앓던 한 여자가 뒤로 다가와서 그분의 겉옷 술을 만졌다.
ko.B: 그때 한 여자가 예수 뒤로 다가왔다. 그 여자는 열두 해 동안 하혈하는 병을 앓고 있었다. 여자는 예수의 겉옷 술을 만졌다.
ko.R: 그때 한 여자가 예수 뒤로 다가왔다. 그 여자는 열두 해 동안 피가 멈추지 않는 병을 앓고 있었다. 여자는 예수의 옷자락을 만졌다.

pt.L: E eis que uma mulher que sofria de hemorragia havia doze anos chegou por trás [{{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}] e tocou a franja do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} manto,
pt.B: Então uma mulher se aproximou por trás {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}. Havia doze anos que ela sofria de hemorragia. Ela tocou a franja do {{deity_pronoun:seu|Seu}} manto.
pt.R: Então uma mulher chegou por trás de Jesus. Fazia doze anos que ela tinha um sangramento. Ela tocou a ponta da roupa {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}.

am.L: እነሆም፣ አሥራ ሁለት ዓመት ደም ሲፈሳት የኖረች አንዲት ሴት ከበስተ ኋላው መጥታ የልብሱን ዘርፍ ነካች፤
am.B: ከዚያም አንዲት ሴት ከኋላው መጣች። ይህች ሴት ለአሥራ ሁለት ዓመት ደም ሲፈሳት ኖራለች። እርሷም የልብሱን ዘርፍ ነካች።
am.R: ከዚያም አንዲት ሴት ከኢየሱስ ኋላ መጣች። ለአሥራ ሁለት ዓመት ደም ይፈሳት ነበር። እሷም የልብሱን ጫፍ ነካች።

decisions.choice: bleeding: a flow of blood that made her ritually unclean
decisions.reason: A woman with such bleeding was unclean, and so was anything she touched (Leviticus 15:25-27). For twelve years she had been cut off from worship.

decisions.choice: the fringe: the tassel worn at the corner of the cloak
decisions.reason: The law told Israelites to wear tassels to remind them of God's commands (Numbers 15:38-39). Jesus wore them.
As in 1:20, Literal uses "look" and Balanced and Readable carry the word's force in the flow of the sentence.
The word is the tassel worn at the corner of the cloak (meaning decision m2). "Kishada" is a tassel; "pindo" is a hem, which loses the picture. Readable says "edge", as the English Readable does.
The tassel worn at the corner of the cloak (meaning decision m2). "Borde" (edge), the familiar word, loses it, so only Readable uses it, as the English Readable says "edge".

decisions.choice: "ra huyết" (L); "bệnh rong huyết" (B); "bệnh ra máu" (R); "bà" for the woman
decisions.reason: As in Mark 5:25, the parallel account.

decisions.choice: "tua áo" (L, B); "mép áo" (R) for the fringe
decisions.reason: The fringe is the tassel the Law told Israelites to wear at the corners of the cloak (meaning decision); "tua" names a tassel. Readable says simply the edge of his clothes, as the English Readable does.

decisions.choice: "피가 흐르는 [병을] 앓다" (L); "하혈하는 병" (B); "피가 멈추지 않는 병" (R)
decisions.reason: Worded as the Korean Mark 5:25, the parallel account; "혈루증" is the word of older versions and not current Korean.
The word is the tassel worn at the corner of the cloak (meaning decision); "술" names it. Readable says the plain "edge of his clothes", as the English Readable does.

"Franja" is the word Portuguese uses for the tassels of Numbers 15:38-39 that the meaning note (m2) refers to; "borla" is a decorative tassel with no link to the law, and "orla" is only the edge. Readable says "a ponta da roupa", as the English Readable says "the edge of his clothes".

decisions.choice: እነሆ (L); ከዚያም or not rendered (B, R)
decisions.reason: እነሆ is the Amharic word that points to what comes next in a story, and Literal keeps it wherever the Greek has its 'look'; ተመልከቱ would sound like a command to the hearers.

source.text: ἔλεγεν γὰρ ἐν ἑαυτῇ· Ἐὰν μόνον ἅψωμαι τοῦ ἱματίου αὐτοῦ σωθήσομαι.

records.literal_gloss: was saying for in herself, If only I touch the garment of him I will be saved.

en.L: for she was saying to herself, "If I only touch {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} garment, I will be saved."
en.B: She thought, "If I can just touch {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} cloak, I will be made well."
en.R: She said to herself, "If I can just touch {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} clothes, I will be healed."

es.L: pues decía en su interior: «Si solo toco {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto, seré salvada».
es.B: Pensaba: «Si logro tocar aunque sea {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} manto, quedaré sana».
es.R: Se decía a sí misma: «Si tan solo toco {{deity_pronoun:su|Su}} ropa, quedaré curada».

fr.L: car elle disait en elle-même : « Si seulement je touche {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} vêtement, je serai sauvée. »
fr.B: Elle pensait : « Si je peux seulement toucher {{deity_pronoun:son|Son}} manteau, je serai guérie. »
fr.R: Elle se disait : « Si je touche juste {{deity_pronoun:ses|Ses}} vêtements, je serai guérie. »

sw.B: Alifikiri, "Hata nikigusa joho {{deity_pronoun:lake|Lake}} tu, nitapona."
sw.R: Alijiambia, "Nikiweza kugusa nguo {{deity_pronoun:zake|Zake}} tu, nitapona."

vi.L: vì bà nói trong lòng: "Nếu tôi chỉ chạm được áo của {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, tôi sẽ được cứu."
vi.B: Bà nghĩ thầm: "Chỉ cần chạm được vào áo choàng {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}}, tôi sẽ được lành."
vi.R: Bà tự nhủ: "Chỉ cần chạm vào áo {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} thôi, tôi sẽ khỏi bệnh."

ko.L: 그 여자가 속으로 "내가 그분의 겉옷만 만져도 구원을 받을 것이다" 하고 말하고 있었기 때문이다.
ko.B: 그 여자는 "그분의 겉옷만 만져도 내가 나을 것이다" 하고 속으로 생각했던 것이다.
ko.R: 여자는 "그분의 옷만 만질 수 있어도 나는 나을 것이다" 하고 혼자 생각했다.

pt.L: pois ela dizia consigo mesma: "Se eu apenas tocar o manto {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, serei salva."
pt.B: Ela pensava: "Se eu conseguir tocar ao menos o manto {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, ficarei curada."
pt.R: Ela dizia a si mesma: "Se eu conseguir só tocar a roupa {{deity_pronoun:dele|Dele}}, vou ser curada."

am.L: በልቧ፦ «ልብሱን ብቻ እንኳ ብነካ እድናለሁ» ትል ነበርና።
am.B: «ልብሱን ብቻ እንኳ ብነካ እድናለሁ» ብላ አስባ ነበር።
am.R: እሷም በልቧ፦ «ልብሱን ብቻ ብነካ እድናለሁ» አለች።

decisions.choice: saved: made well, and more than that, rescued
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used in 1:21 ("he will save his people"). Here it means healing, but Matthew's readers hear the wider sense of being rescued by Jesus.
Literal keeps the word's wider sense; Balanced and Readable say what she hoped for, and the meaning note explains the rest.

The verb means to be made well and more than that, rescued (meaning decision m1). "Kuokoka" means both to recover and to be saved, so Literal keeps the double sense, as in John 11:12; Balanced and Readable say what she hoped for. The same in verse 22.

decisions.choice: seré salvada (L); quedaré sana (B); quedaré curada (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the verb "salvar", which says more than getting well (meaning decision m1); Balanced and Readable say what she hoped for. The same in verse 22.
As in Mark 5:28 and 5:34: the verb means "saved" and here also "made well" (meaning decision); Literal keeps "cứu", the other levels say what she hoped for. The same in 9:22.

As the Korean Mark 5:23-34: the verb means both being made well and being rescued (meaning decision). Literal keeps "구원" so the link with salvation shows; Balanced and Readable say what happened to her body.
She speaks of Jesus, not to him; "seu" could be read as "your", so Portuguese says "dele", which also carries the deity_pronoun setting.

decisions.choice: እድናለሁ (I will be saved, made well) at every level
alternatives: እፈወሳለሁ (I will be healed), as the English Balanced and Readable say
decisions.reason: Amharic ዳነ means both to recover from an illness and to be saved, just as the Greek word does, so one word keeps both senses at every level where English has to choose between 'saved', 'made well' and 'healed'.

source.text: ὁ δὲ Ἰησοῦς στραφεὶς καὶ ἰδὼν αὐτὴν εἶπεν· Θάρσει, θύγατερ· ἡ πίστις σου σέσωκέν σε.

records.literal_gloss: The but Jesus having turned and having seen her said, Take courage, daughter; the faith of you has saved you.

en.L: But Jesus turned, and seeing her, said, "Take heart, daughter; your faith has saved you."
en.B: Jesus turned around, and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} saw her, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, "Courage, my daughter! Your faith has made you well."
en.R: Jesus turned and saw her. He said, "Cheer up, my daughter! You are healed because of your faith."

es.L: Pero Jesús se volvió y, al verla, dijo: «¡Ánimo, hija! Tu fe te ha salvado».
es.B: Jesús se dio vuelta y, al verla, le dijo: «¡Ánimo, hija mía! Tu fe te ha devuelto la salud».
es.R: Jesús se volvió y la vio. Le dijo: «¡Anímate, hija mía! Estás sana gracias a tu fe».

fr.L: Mais Jésus, s’étant retourné et l’ayant vue, dit : « Courage, fille ; ta foi t’a sauvée. »
fr.B: Jésus se retourna et, quand {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} la vit, {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} lui dit : « Courage, ma fille ! Ta foi t’a guérie. »
fr.R: Jésus s’est retourné et {{deity_pronoun:il|Il}} l’a vue. Il lui a dit : « Courage, ma fille ! Tu es guérie grâce à ta foi. »

sw.L: Lakini Yesu, akigeuka na kumwona, akasema, "Jipe moyo, binti; imani yako imekuokoa."
sw.B: Yesu aligeuka, na alipomwona, akasema, "Uwe hodari, binti yangu! Imani yako imekufanya mzima."
sw.R: Yesu aligeuka, akamwona. Akasema, "Changamka, binti yangu! Umepona kwa sababu ya imani yako."

vi.L: Nhưng Đức Giê-xu quay lại, thấy bà thì nói: "Hãy vững lòng, con gái; đức tin của con đã cứu con."
vi.B: Đức Giê-xu quay lại, và khi thấy bà, {{deity_pronoun:ngài|Ngài}} nói: "Con gái ơi, hãy vững lòng! Đức tin của con đã làm cho con được lành."
vi.R: Đức Giê-xu quay lại và thấy bà. Ngài nói: "Con gái ơi, hãy vui lên! Con được lành bệnh vì con có đức tin."

ko.L: 그러나 예수께서 돌아서서 그 여자를 보시고 말씀하셨다. "딸아, 안심하여라. 네 믿음이 너를 구원하였다."
ko.B: 예수께서 돌아서서 그 여자를 보시고 말씀하셨다. "딸아, 용기를 내라. 네 믿음이 너를 낫게 하였다."
ko.R: 예수께서 돌아서서 그 여자를 보셨다. 그리고 말씀하셨다. "내 딸아, 힘을 내라. 네가 믿었기 때문에 병이 나았다."

pt.L: Mas Jesus, voltando-se e vendo-a, disse: "Tenha ânimo, filha; a sua fé a salvou."
pt.B: Jesus se virou e, quando a viu, disse: "Coragem, minha filha! A sua fé a curou."
pt.R: Jesus se virou e olhou para ela. Ele disse: "Ânimo, minha filha! Você foi curada por causa da sua fé."

am.L: ኢየሱስ ግን ዘወር ብሎ አያትና እንዲህ አለ፦ «አይዞሽ፣ ልጅ ሆይ፤ እምነትሽ አድኖሻል።»
am.B: ኢየሱስም ዘወር ብሎ ባያት ጊዜ እንዲህ አላት፦ «ልጄ ሆይ፣ አይዞሽ! እምነትሽ አድኖሻል።»
am.R: ኢየሱስ ዘወር ብሎ አያት። እንዲህም አላት፦ «ልጄ ሆይ፣ አይዞሽ! ስላመንሽ ድነሻል።»

decisions.choice: saved: made well, and more than that, rescued

decisions.choice: daughter: a warm address that takes her into God's family
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks to an outcast woman as a member of the family.
As in 9:21.
A bare "fille" as an address sounds abrupt in French; "ma fille" carries the warmth the meaning note (m2) describes, as in Mark 5:34 and Luke 8:48.
As in Mark 5:34: the address is warm and takes her into God's family (meaning decision); Vietnamese "con gái" and "con" say the same, while the narrator calls her "bà".
"딸아" is warm and fits Jesus's plain style, as in the Korean Mark 5:34; it takes her into God's family (meaning decision). The call to take courage is worded more plainly at each level.

en.L: And the woman was saved from that hour.
en.B: And from that moment the woman was well.
en.R: The woman was healed from that moment.

es.L: Y fue salvada la mujer desde aquella hora.
es.B: Y desde ese momento la mujer quedó sana.
es.R: La mujer quedó curada en ese mismo momento.

fr.L: Et la femme fut sauvée dès cette heure-là.
fr.B: Et dès ce moment, la femme fut guérie.
fr.R: À partir de ce moment, la femme a été guérie.

sw.B: Na tangu wakati huo mwanamke yule akawa mzima.

vi.R: Ngay lúc đó, bà được lành bệnh.

ko.B: 그 순간부터 그 여자는 나았다.
ko.R: 바로 그때부터 그 여자의 병이 나았다.

pt.L: E a mulher foi salva desde aquela hora.
pt.B: E a partir daquele momento a mulher ficou curada.
pt.R: Daquele momento em diante, a mulher estava curada.

am.L: ሴቲቱም ከዚያች ሰዓት ጀምሮ ዳነች።
am.B: ከዚያች ቅጽበት ጀምሮ ሴቲቱ ዳነች።
am.R: ሴቲቱ ከዚያን ጊዜ ጀምሮ ዳነች።

decisions.choice: saved: made well, and more than that, rescued
